findings.claim: 'The Catholic Catechism describes popular piety as “a true treasure of the People of God.”'
findings.truth: The phrase comes from the Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy (2001), which attributes it to the Magisterium (section 9 and section 61). The Catechism paragraphs on popular piety (1674-1676) do not use it.
findings.evidence: vatican.va, Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy, sections 9 and 61

findings.claim: 6-mark key: 'the Catholic Catechism calls popular piety ‘a true treasure of the People of God’'.
findings.truth: Same misattribution as F1; the source is the Directory on Popular Piety.
findings.evidence: vatican.va, Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy

findings.claim: 'Jesus warns against “babbling on like pagans” (Matthew 6:7)'.
findings.truth: Matthew 6:7 (NIV) reads 'And when you pray, do not keep on babbling like pagans'. 'Babbling on like pagans' is no translation's wording.

findings.claim: 12-mark key: "Jesus himself warned against 'babbling on' in formal repetition".
findings.truth: Same misquote as F3.

findings.claim: Flashcard 10 answer: 'He warned against babbling on like pagans'.
findings.truth: Same misquote as F3.

findings.claim: Question 6 is typed '2 marks — State / Give' and its key awards '1 mark for each valid point (up to 2 marks total)'.
findings.truth: This paper sets two five-part questions of 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks per religion. No 2-mark part exists. Re-cast as the 4-mark Explain.

findings.claim: 'the Grotto de Massabielle'.
findings.truth: The site is the grotto of Massabielle (French: grotte de Massabielle). 'Grotto de' is neither.

findings.claim: 'This contrast between Catholic and Protestant views on pilgrimage is a significant mark-scheme point.'
findings.truth: An invented claim about a mark scheme. The requirement is spec content: 'different Christian views about the importance of pilgrimage'.

findings.claim: 'the belief that God heals (John 11:25 — ‘I am the resurrection and the life’)'.
findings.truth: John 11:25 is a resurrection saying, not a healing text. The verse is right for the funeral rite, wrong for healing.

findings.claim: Question 6 typed '2 marks — State / Give'.
findings.truth: No 2-mark part exists on this paper (1, 1, 4, 6, 12). Re-cast as the 4-mark Explain.

findings.claim: Gaudium et Spes opening quoted as 'The joys and hopes, the griefs and anxieties of the people of this age... these too are the joys and hopes...'.
findings.truth: The Vatican English text reads 'The joys and the hopes, the griefs and the anxieties of the men of this age, especially those who are poor or in any way afflicted, these are the joys and hopes, the griefs and anxieties of the followers of Christ.'

findings.claim: Trocaire glossary definition: 'named after the Irish for ‘Lord’ (Trocaire = mercy)'.
findings.truth: Trocaire is the Irish word for mercy or compassion. It has nothing to do with the Irish for 'Lord'. The definition also contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: the lesson's own prose and glossary_terms entry; Irish 'trocaire' = mercy

findings.claim: 'CSAN — Catholic Social Action Network'.
findings.truth: CSAN is Caritas Social Action Network, the social action agency of the Catholic Church in England and Wales, formed in 2003.

findings.claim: 'the UN Declaration of Human Rights (1948)'.
findings.truth: Its name is the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948).
findings.evidence: UN, Universal Declaration of Human Rights

findings.claim: Question 6 typed '2 marks — State / Give'.
findings.truth: No 2-mark part exists on this paper (1, 1, 4, 6, 12). Re-cast as the 4-mark Explain.

findings.claim: 'There are approximately five million Catholics in England and Wales, making Catholicism the largest single Christian denomination.'
findings.truth: The Church of England is the largest denomination in England and Wales. Catholicism is the second largest single church.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Catholic Church in England and Wales ('the second largest single church if Christianity is divided into separate denominations')

findings.claim: 'to share the faith winsmomely without coercion'.
findings.truth: 'Winsmomely' is not a word. Replaced with 'attractively', which a 15-year-old will read.

findings.claim: Question 6 typed '2 marks — State / Give'.
findings.truth: No 2-mark part exists on this paper (1, 1, 4, 6, 12). Re-cast as the 4-mark Explain.

findings.claim: Every lesson's question 6 opens with a named-person scenario ('Anya, a Catholic teenager in a parish in Leeds...', 'Mrs Nguyen travels to Lourdes...', 'Jerome is a member of his local SVP conference...').
findings.truth: This paper sets no scenario stems; the form belongs to other boards. Option A: leave the stems, because after the mark relabel each reads as a valid 4-mark Explain and the stem only adds context. Option B: strip the stems so the practice bank matches the paper exactly. Recommendation: A.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.1; the four practice banks in this unit
findings.ruling: Leave: scenario stems read as valid 4-mark Explain after the relabel.

findings.claim: 'Pope Francis’s description of a “Church of the poor”'.
findings.truth: Francis's own words are 'a Church which is poor and for the poor' (Evangelii Gaudium 198). 'Church of the poor' is closer to John XXIII. Not edited: the paragraph text could not be confirmed this session.
findings.evidence: vatican.va fetch of Evangelii Gaudium returned a truncated text

findings.claim: 'approximately five million Catholics in England and Wales'.
findings.truth: The Bishops' Conference reports about 6.2 million baptised members (2023); census self-identification is lower. The range is wide, so no single true value; the figure is left alone.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Catholic Church in England and Wales

findings.claim: 'HCPT (Handicapped Children’s Pilgrimage Trust)'.
findings.truth: The charity is now styled HCPT - The Pilgrimage Trust. The old expansion is historically accurate, so it is not wrong, only dated.

findings.claim: Lesson descriptions run 104-113 characters (all four lessons).
findings.truth: The house limit is under 100 characters. Pre-existing, and not a fact error, so not edited here.

summary: Four lessons, 23 findings, 26 edits. Four quoted or attributed texts were wrong: the Catechism was credited with a phrase from the Directory on Popular Piety, Matthew 6:7 was misquoted three times, the Gaudium et Spes opening line was reworded, and CSAN was expanded as Catholic rather than Caritas Social Action Network. Catholicism was called the largest denomination in England and Wales when it is the second largest. Every lesson's sixth practice question was typed as a 2-mark part, which this paper does not set.
